figure_caption: Information boundaries of budgeted score prediction. Sparse historical scores support the global factor fit and historical-only cross-fitted donor calibration, including a zero-blend option. Frozen factors and previously selected indices determine queries within the permitted reservoir; revealed score values condition the new-model latent profile and overlap-aware donor weights but do not change query ordering or fitted historical state. Donor-excluded residuals are combined by a weighted median, shrunk by effective donor count, blended with the global base, and clipped; queried entries are not residual-adjusted. The entire query reservoir is disjoint from the fixed sealed target set, whose scores and mask remain evaluator-only. Only completed predictions cross to target scoring. The schematic describes the evaluated computation, not measured component-specific benefit.

panels.title: Budgeted prediction and information boundaries
panels.short_caption: Historical-only fitting and nested cross-fitted calibration produce frozen global and donor state. Index-only acquisition exposes a budgeted set of scores for conditioning and local residual transfer. Sealed targets never enter the predictor; no component-specific performance attribution is implied.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: frozen sparse-history fitting and historical-only cross-fitted calibration support budgeted score prediction, while sealed target data remain exclusively with the evaluator.

Use ONE connected full-width information-flow diagram, not independent subpanels. Arrange three adjacent regions: HIST (historical fitting, left about 31% of width), PRED (budgeted prediction, middle about 52%), EVAL (evaluator only, right about 17%). Preserve large readable type rather than explanatory prose. All region containers are non-computational boundaries, not trainable nodes. HIST has a one-way frozen-state handoff to PRED; EVAL has a very conspicuous sealed vertical boundary. No aesthetic colors, fills, or palette are prescribed. No panel letters are needed.

Nodes and their semantic encodings:
HIST: region label 'Historical only'. H: sharp data-array box, label 'Sparse score matrix', small symbols '$$Y,\Omega$$', with a schematic 5-row by 7-column cell array, row-axis name 'Models', column-axis name 'Task/subset columns'. Use two nonnumeric cell treatments, one with a small point for an observed entry and one empty for missing; a tiny key reads 'Observed' and 'Missing'. This is a categorical mask illustration, not a heatmap, quantitative plot, or literal matrix dimensions; build it with native cells, no placeholder. Do not fill holes or put zeros into missing cells.
A: rounded trainable historical process, label 'Ridge ALS'. F: frozen cylinder store, label 'Global factors', symbol '$$\mu,V$$', small tag 'Frozen'.
C: rounded trainable historical process, label 'Cross-fitted calibration'. Include two small overlapping fold-card glyphs inside C, label 'Nested fold exclusion', and a short tag 'Zero blend option'. The cards denote historical validation and donor exclusion, not held-out new-model scores. C includes historical simulated queries, nested donor exclusion, tuning and the final donor-bank rebuild; explain those details in captions rather than on the canvas.
D: frozen cylinder store, label 'Cross-fitted donors', a short symbol line '$$h,\tau,\alpha$$', small tag 'Frozen'. D represents historical donor observations plus fold-excluded auxiliary fits and selected calibration parameters, not precomputed new-model target data.

PRED: region label 'Budgeted prediction'. P: rounded inference process, label 'Integrated-variance queries', budget tag '$$k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$$'. P is not trainable; its selected-index memory is represented by one small self-return arrow, not score feedback. R: sharp data-strip box, label 'Query reservoir', symbol '$$R_\star$$'. R contains a short row of queryable-cell tiles and no sealed cells; it represents new-model queryable data, not the full hidden row. A selected tile has an index marker, but no fabricated numeric score. Q: sharp data box, label 'Revealed scores', symbol '$$y_{\star,Q_k}$$', result of budgeted acquisition, not trainable. B: rounded inference process, label 'Ridge conditioning', short output symbol '$$b_\star$$'; this includes clipping of the global base before adjustment. W: rounded inference process, label 'Overlap-aware weights', short output symbol '$$w_i$$'; scores affect W, not P. M: rounded inference process, label 'Weighted residual median'; includes Q-indexed donor residual lookup from frozen donor-excluded fits. S: rounded inference process, label 'Effective-count shrinkage', second short label 'Calibrated blend'; this applies tau and alpha to the median, with no update to historical state. J: small circular plus glyph, label only '+'; it combines base and correction, not a trainable operation. K: rounded inference process, label 'Clip [0,1]'; K operates on adjusted unqueried entries only, with queried entries excluded from residual correction. O: sharp output data box, label 'Predicted profile', symbol '$$\widehat y_\star$$'; result, not trainable.

EVAL: region label 'Evaluator only'. T: sharp sealed data box, label 'Sealed targets', symbol '$$T_\star$$', with a native lock glyph and small noun-phrase tag 'Fixed across budgets'. The target mask and scores stay inside this region. E: rounded non-trainable process, label 'Target scoring'. Show no metric value, performance bar, or outcome claim. No target data are exposed through R or any other predictor node.

Every edge, exhaustively (all directed): H -> A solid, no label; A -> F solid, no label; H -> C solid, no label; C -> D solid, no label. F -> P solid, no label; F -> B solid, no label. R -> P solid, label '$$R_\star$$' (indices only, not scores); P -> R solid, label '$$Q_k$$' (query request); P -> P dashed short self-return, label '$$Q$$' (earlier selected indices only). Keep these three routes spatially distinct, never a reciprocal score-feedback arrow. R -> Q solid, no label (only requested answers). Q -> B solid, no label; Q -> W solid, no label. D -> W solid, no label (historical anchor observations and bandwidth); D -> M solid, label '$$e_{ij}(Q)$$' (residuals obtained through frozen auxiliary-fit lookup, not held-out targets). Q -> M dashed, label '$$Q_k$$' (only queried indices condition the donor residual lookup; Q's score values do not train donor state). W -> M solid, label '$$w_i$$'. M -> S solid, no label. D -> S solid, label '$$\tau,\alpha$$'. B -> J solid, label '$$b_\star$$'; S -> J solid, label '$$\delta$$'; J -> K solid, no label; K -> O solid, no label. O -> E solid, no label, the ONLY edge crossing into EVAL; T -> E solid, no label, entirely evaluator-side. There are NO other edges, and absolutely no EVAL-to-PRED or EVAL-to-HIST edge, not even dashed. Dashed means auxiliary conditioning, not gradients.

Spatial layout: H at the top of HIST; A/F form a compact left historical lane and C/D a parallel right historical lane beneath H. Make C tall enough for its short fold-exclusion and zero-blend labels. In PRED put P then R across the upper band; Q immediately below R. Beneath these put B in the left base lane and W -> M -> S in the right residual lane, with both lanes converging at J in the lower band, followed by K and O. Route F's two outgoing edges along the left/top margins of PRED. Route D's weight, median, and shrinkage inputs through short grouped fan-outs below the acquisition band; use orthogonal routes and avoid crossing node interiors. Give the index-only R -> P route a different side from the request P -> R route. At right, T sits above E, with O adjacent to E across the sealed boundary. The boundary must separate all target cells from the query reservoir, not merely separate selected queries from targets. Keep targets spatially detached from the reservoir; do not draw a visible full new-model score row linking them. Small line-style key 'Forward data' and 'Auxiliary indices' can sit beneath the connected diagram. No disconnected inset.

Importance ranking: (1) sparse observed/missing matrix and the non-crossable sealed-target boundary; (2) budgeted index selection versus revealed answers, with no answer-to-policy feedback; (3) historical-only calibration and both frozen stores; (4) global base plus locally weighted cross-fitted residual correction; (5) evaluator scoring without any measured outcome. Use glyphs and structure instead of formulas. Draw NO raw multi-term equation and NO plot. The plus glyph with two inbound labeled edges is mandatory.

Exact text budget, allowing repetition of the same short label only where specified: 'Historical only'; 'Sparse score matrix'; '$$Y,\Omega$$'; 'Models'; 'Task/subset columns'; 'Observed'; 'Missing'; 'Ridge ALS'; 'Global factors'; '$$\mu,V$$'; 'Frozen' (on F and D); 'Cross-fitted calibration'; 'Nested fold exclusion'; 'Zero blend option'; 'Cross-fitted donors'; '$$h,\tau,\alpha$$'; 'Budgeted prediction'; 'Integrated-variance queries'; '$$k\in\{1,2,4,8\}$$'; 'Query reservoir'; '$$R_\star$$' (R and index-only edge); 'Revealed scores'; '$$y_{\star,Q_k}$$'; 'Ridge conditioning'; '$$b_\star$$' (B and its outgoing edge); 'Overlap-aware weights'; '$$w_i$$' (W and its outgoing edge); 'Weighted residual median'; 'Effective-count shrinkage'; 'Calibrated blend'; '+'; 'Clip [0,1]'; 'Predicted profile'; '$$\widehat y_\star$$'; 'Evaluator only'; 'Sealed targets'; '$$T_\star$$'; 'Fixed across budgets'; 'Target scoring'; '$$Q_k$$' (request and lookup edges); '$$Q$$'; '$$e_{ij}(Q)$$'; '$$\tau,\alpha$$'; '$$\delta$$'; 'Forward data'; 'Auxiliary indices'. No other explanatory sentence, numeric score, improvement claim, gain arrow, trainable new-model parameter update, or component-attribution label appears on canvas.
